what_happened: Dispatch text states meta-builder-agent.md's Stage 1 'has no resolution step of its own to correct' and frames remedy (b) as adding a new resolution step, and separately calls the agent's existing behavior a 'silent cwd fallback'. Git history shows Stage 1 already carries a Defensive fallback (added same-day as skill-meta's own gap acknowledgment, well before both the 2026-10-11 and 2026-11-05 diagnosis dates) that resolves $TARGET_ROOT via ${CLAUDE_AGENT_GLOBAL_ROOT:-$HOME/.config/nvim} and explicitly forbids CWD as a fallback. The real gap is not absence of a resolution step but its unenforced, silent, prose-only compliance -- the Nov-5 recurrence happened despite this fallback already being written.

Enumerated every direct meta-builder-agent dispatcher via two differently-shaped greps (broad text mention, then literal subagent_type token) and found exactly 3 call sites: skill-meta/SKILL.md (correct), context/patterns/telemetry-meta-submode.md (correct), context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md Step 4b (broken, no target_root). Confirms the dispatch's own claim that remedy (a) alone would have sufficed for the measured Nov-5 instance.

The research report's own idiom for the skill-meta discharge finding ('already discharged', 'now stale', 'a gap that has not existed since July') is exactly the record-versioning language that no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md forbids, and agent-system/** is not exempt (only specs/** is). Copying the report's framing into the deliverable would fail check-record-versioning.sh. The plan adds an explicit high-likelihood risk row and makes the lint a per-phase verification step rather than deferring it to the final gate.

The research report's Decisions section was directly actionable at plan time: it pre-settled both plan-time scope questions (accept postflight-tool-restrictions.md, reject commands/meta.md) with reasoning, and its stale-premise finding reshaped remedy (b) from 'add a resolution step' to 'strengthen an existing one'. Planning needed only live re-verification of the cited line ranges, not re-investigation; all seven candidate targets and the three-dispatcher enumeration confirmed on first pass.

Phase 4's verification criterion 'validate-context-budgets.sh passes' cannot be satisfied as a whole-script exit: the script reports 10 violations repo-wide (agent token-budget overages on agents never touched by this task -- general-implementation-agent OVER:40368, neovim-implementation-agent OVER:11640, nix-research-agent OVER:4056, planner-agent OVER:14416, etc. -- plus 3 dead context-index entries and 1 pre-existing double-loading classification on the exact narrative file this phase edited). Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this phase's edit by inspecting a worktree at the pre-dispatch commit (2530aa165) and by checking that none of the overaged agents are in this task's file_scope. The actually-relevant sub-check for this phase's eager-loaded rule-file addition -- the Tier 1 (always-loaded) budget check -- reports Status: OK (334/500 lines), and test-context-reachability.sh and check-record-versioning.sh both pass on the edited paths. Discharging Phase 4 verification against the narrower, actually-applicable checks rather than the whole-script exit code.
